doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Blakey and Getz encourage her writing; who played her music
summary: Blakey and Getz urged her to write; mostly rhythm sections played her music at first, then horn players like Michael Brecker; Getz featured her trio.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did he encourage you to write for the band?

He was always telling me to write for the band but so was Stan Getz and I think that the only people that wanted to play my music were the rhythm sections. It was a long time before horn players came in and wanted to play. I think maybe one of the first was Mike Brecker. He’s on one of my first albums. He loved it. And then after that, now I have no problem. Not that everyone wants to do that but there is maybe five or six people that really — I’ve had Greg Osby do some things, Javon Jackson, Ravi Coltrane, Chris Potter was on one album, so, and there’s more, I don’t want to forget them but I can’t think of everyone at once. But in those days mainly the trios just wanted to play my music. So Stan tried a few times. Then what he did was actually feature the trio at the beginning of each set and we would play.
Now he was not a music reader, was he? He could read some?
He could read, I heard he didn’t but he could.
Okay. Maybe he preferred not to.
My tunes were a little bit more than what he wanted to get into.
